topics.label: Lecture framing and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the class and sets out the lecture's aims before introducing its subject matter.

topics.label: Tumor viruses and the discovery and testing of cellular transforming genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how tumor viruses revealed cellular transforming genes and how the genes' capacity to transform cells can be tested.

topics.label: Functional effects of cancer mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics classify cancer mutations by their effects on tumor growth and illustrate how those effects operate through cell-cycle control and mutation-specific gene function.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish forms of genetic instability and explain how defects in DNA repair, replication, and mitosis produce them and affect cancer cells.

topics.label: Mutation timing in colorectal cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines when mutations and chromosomal instability arise as colorectal tumors progress.

topics.label: Hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inherited mutations in genes controlling genomic integrity or growth control predispose people to cancer.

topics.label: BRCA2 restoration and the persistence of malignancy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic shows that a tumor can remain lethal after BRCA2 function is restored, so ongoing genetic instability is not required for malignancy.

topics.label: Lecture close and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by inviting questions, recommending reading, and previewing the next lecture.
